A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIRD framework and share identifiable methods, experiments, and appendix material. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are sufficiently readable for reliable comparison, including the image-based prompts in v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original probability-estimation evaluations, decision-making experiments, transfer-training results, component ablations, and human preferences for generated follow-up questions.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for both Llama-2 and Llama-3.1, alongside transfer-training and human evaluations. Its appendices also report dataset quality checks, error analysis, and an annotation pilot.

M1.justification: The Bayesian aggregation, training losses, and Algorithm 1 remain substantially unchanged. However, v1's hierarchical/direct entailment ensemble is replaced by direct entailment with self-correction in v2 Section 3.4. Follow-up generation also changes from randomly selecting an unobserved factor to selecting the most important one and its highest-probability outcome-aligned value (v1 A.10; v2 A.9). These are localized procedural refinements.

E1.justification: The benchmark suite remains COMMON2SENSE, TODAY, PLASMA, MATRES, and TRACIE. Within PLASMA, v2 introduces generated conditions supporting manually identified less-common outcomes, revising the represented planning situations (A.4). Figure 1 also replaces restaurant and flight examples with a constrained charging-station planning case. Coverage changes within the existing broad domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds logit-based probability baselines and Llama-3.1 Vanilla, CoT, and EC comparisons. Its BIRD ablation rows switch from Llama-2 to Llama-3.1, although Llama-2 ablations remain in Table 2. Figure 1 replaces the illustrative GPT-4 comparison with OpenAI o1. The principal existing comparison approaches are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-3.1-70B as an experimental backbone. The probability-evaluation annotation pool changes from 400 to 450 examples; v2 obtains 366 agreement-qualified examples and filters these to 350 on which every evaluated method makes correct binary decisions, unlike v1's stated selection process. PLASMA is reconstructed as 1,395 instances across 279 scenarios rather than 1,357 instances. Follow-up evaluation instructions also shift toward informing the choice between outcomes (Figure 4). These materially revise the reported evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses addressing several previously untested questions: failure attribution for BIRD-wrong/CoT-correct cases (Table 4), comparative factor quality across backbones (Table 5), human verification of generated datasets (A.4), and the feasibility of absolute-probability annotation (A.5). It also extends factor-generation ablations to Llama-3.1 in Table 7. The earlier pepper example is retained as Table 6, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed replication, across-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both use point estimates and vote-based aggregation. The added annotation-quality outcomes do not introduce uncertainty estimates for the reported model comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces Llama-2 BIRD's reported F1 of 0.651 with 0.592 and adds Llama-3.1 results, including 0.588 for optimized BIRD. Table 2 reports PLASMA BIRD/CoT accuracies of 74.0/76.8 instead of 92.0/99.6; Table 3 revises its PLASMA scores and averages. Follow-up preferences change from 126 wins, 40 ties, and 84 losses to 132, 36, and 82. New diagnostic results are also reported. Changed procedures and data prevent treating these as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equation 4 replaces v1's equality identifying the conditional probability with the opinion-pool estimate with estimated-probability notation and an approximation sign, qualifying its mathematical status. The marginalization derivation in A.1, weak-ordering and noninteraction assumptions in A.2, and optimization equations otherwise remain unchanged; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains interpretable, controllable probability estimation through BIRD. The headline advantage changes from 35% over GPT-4, with over 65% human alignment, to approximately 30% over LLM baselines. The introduction and conclusion strengthen the decision-making claim from performance comparable to CoT to outperforming CoT, supported particularly by the added Llama-3.1 experiments.

C2.justification: v2 explains why rankings alone can be insufficient for constrained planning and why relative human judgments are used instead of absolute probabilities, citing its inconclusive annotation pilot. It attributes Llama-3.1's stronger decisions partly to more comprehensive factors. The unrestricted applicability discussion, including hierarchical handling of multiple outcomes, is omitted. Unknown predictions and the proposed CoT fallback remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies previously undocumented prompts for Vanilla, probability CoT, EC, and decision-making CoT baselines (Figures 11–14), plus the self-correction prompt. It specifies greedy decoding at temperature 0 for the logit baseline and provides additional dataset-construction and verification details. Core optimization hyperparameters and the training pseudocode were already present; no code-release information is added.

R1.justification: Related work is substantively broadened with a probabilistic-inference subsection discussing uncertain NLI, ThinkSum, and probabilistic language-of-thought approaches. v2 explicitly positions BIRD against these methods through incomplete-information handling and interpretability, and identifies Hou et al. (2024) as a close uncertainty-decomposition comparison. Decomposition and uncertainty-sampling coverage also expands beyond v1.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around incomplete information and constrained planning. Modeling is reorganized to introduce marginalization earlier and present Bayesian parameter optimization before entailment. Experimental explanations and related work are substantially rewritten, and appendix sections are reorganized. These changes reshape the narrative beyond merely inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redesigned around charging-station planning. Main comparison tables and the factor-generation ablation table gain structures for two backbones, and new error-analysis and factor-comparison tables appear. Appendix prompt screenshots become consistently styled text boxes, with additional prompt figures. Typography, headings, and page composition also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical support and auditability through a second backbone, logit comparisons, dataset checks, diagnostic analyses, and fuller prompt documentation. The clearer organization also helps explain the existing framework. However, the central evaluation still measures filtered relative judgments rather than validating the absolute probabilities motivating the planning example. v2 also introduces a reproducibility inconsistency: Section 4.2 assigns the 1/2 ablation a fallback probability of 0, while Appendix A.6 retains 1/2. The additions support a net improvement, but these limitations constrain its significance.
